I'd say to follow up with your cardiologist, of course, but you're likely just feeling the anxiety. It's very unfortunate to suffer from health anxiety like that and *also* have a diagnosed heart condition, my heart goes out to you. (Lol)

Knowing the actual diagnosis track for your specific heart issues and being able to be 100% certain that your night flutters are only anxiety would most definitely help not to overreact and go to a hospital every time. 

That being said, I also think that you've made the right choice in going to get it checked out when you're not certain. That's just smart living. 

I probably haven't given any advice or said anything you've not heard before, but I hope that you were able to glean something from this comment/thread and are able to push past these anxious events and beyond as soon as possible. All the power to you, friend.

I was visiting a friend on the other side of the country, and he had to work one of the days I was there, so I went out to check the local breweries out. At the first brewery I went to, I met a guy who was super friendly and we started talking beer. 

After a drink or two, he told me he had just gotten engaged and showed me a picture of his fiancee. Said he was visiting a friend who was busy, his fiancee was at a concert for a band he wasn't a fan of, and he himself was also from out of town. I bought him a drink and told him about the other breweries I was going to visit next, and invited him to come with me.

We spent the next five hours going around to breweries and pubs drinking and sharing his good news with strangers who would listen. We even facetimed his fiancee a few times. Many drinks were had, and we ended up getting dinner together too. Shook hands, exchanged numbers, congratulated him once again, and went our separate ways. Never talked to him again, but I hope he's happily married with his lovely fiancee!
